paragraphs: Here's what I see in David's last words, friend. A man near the end of his life doesn't talk about his own glory. He hands his son a charge: "So be strong and prove yourself a man," and "keep the charge of the LORD your God to walk in His ways" (1 Kings 2:2-3). Strength in this passage isn't muscles. It's walking God's way, and David says that's how Solomon will prosper in all he does (1 Kings 2:3).

Then David says the LORD's promise to him depends on how his descendants live: "If your descendants take heed to walk faithfully before Me with all their heart and soul, you will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel" (1 Kings 2:4). So David passes on more than a crown. He passes on a way of life, and he wants Solomon to walk it with ALL his heart and soul. The rest of David's charge, the hard words about Joab and Shimei and the kindness for Barzillai's sons, is David telling Solomon what he thinks wisdom looks like. I think he wants Solomon to remember who stood by him and who didn't, and to act on it (1 Kings 2:5-9).

So what does that mean for you, baker? Whatever you hand to the people after you, a kitchen, a job, a family, a habit, what you hand them is mostly how you lived. David's reign lasted forty years, and then it was done (1 Kings 2:10-11). What carried on was the charge to walk with the LORD, and Solomon's throne was firmly established (1 Kings 2:12). This story isn't over yet, so keep your apron on and watch how Solomon carries that charge.
